title: Assessing Covariate-Informed Grid Load Forecasting with a Time-Series Foundation Model

primary_sources.paraphrase: arXiv record (v1, 2026-09-06; presented at IJCNN 2026). Chronos-2 on ISO New England and ENTSO-E load against task-specific deep models: fine-tuning helps a lot and it does well at short horizons, but zero-shot it trails those models and its error grows faster with horizon. No code link.

Full text. Daily series (ENTSO-E as daily peak), one-year test splits, horizons of 30, 60 and 90 days, 30-day history, MAPE. Calendar and weather covariates over history and horizon; TCN, LSTM and Transformer baselines trained per dataset. Tables III and IV give means over five seeds; no intervals, code or data statement. Hourly week-ahead is left as future work.

Commit history of amazon/chronos-2, the study's central model: weights and config added in commit 95a9710e on 2025-10-30; later commits are README, tag and deployment-guide changes by title. The repository's metadata lists the licence as apache-2.0.

relevance.rationale: Electric load at zone and country level, but daily (ENTSO-E as daily peak), not hourly; the scale has no exact slot for daily load, so 2. Horizons are 30 to 90 days in daily steps, far from a 168-hour week (1). Temperature and other weather are supplied over the forecast horizon as known-future inputs (3), though the paper does not say whether they are observed or forecast values.

checks.notes: pre_registered: the paper mentions no pre-registration and has one arXiv version. training_overlap_risk is about our run: the amazon/chronos-2 weights were committed on 2025-10-30 (commit 95a9710e, identified by its title; model.safetensors is in the repository's file list but the commit's own file list was not inspected), before the first scored week (2025-11-10), so all scored weeks start after it. independent_replication: two searches found no replication and no author code. Central model: Chronos-2 (zero-shot, LoRA and full fine-tuning); TCN, LSTM and Transformer trained per dataset are the others. Evidence is weak by the spec: numbers without code, although the source data are public, each test split is 365 days and five seeds were run; tables give means only. baseline_same_inputs is 'yes' because the baselines are described as taking the target and covariate series with the same 30-day history; the paper does not explicitly confirm an identical covariate set or calendar encoding, and the baselines were trained on years of the target series while zero-shot Chronos-2 was not. Unverified: how ISO-NE load was aggregated to daily; whether future weather is observed or forecast (not stated); the Chronos-2 checkpoint revision; whether the datasets overlap Chronos-2 pre-training data (the ENTSO-E set comes from fev-bench; not discussed); which cells the paper marks as best. Table values were read from the arXiv HTML through two fetch summaries that agree, not from the PDF. The text says full fine-tuning always beats LoRA, but two table cells without covariates show the reverse by 0.05 points. Authors are at GE Vernova research. The write-up is CC BY-NC-SA; the licence field is that of the Chronos-2 weights.

label: ACCEPT_STAGE3
label_reason: Sourced study of our primary-comparison model, Chronos-2 with weather covariates, on electric load, but its headline comparison (fine-tuned Chronos-2 against deep models trained per dataset, daily data, 30 to 90 days ahead) cannot be re-measured with a model in runnable_models: it needs fine-tuning and trained baselines, which is work beyond an adapter. Only its side findings (zero-shot gain from covariates, error growth with horizon) map onto rows we already have, and the published numbers come without code or intervals.
implementation_hint: Runnable today: Chronos-2 zero-shot with temperature via models/chronos2.py, weights amazon/chronos-2 (weights commit 95a9710e2596287d08352589f42634fa5abdf0a7, 2025-10-30); its with-temperature and univariate rows and the error by lead hour within 168 h are the nearest analogue of the paper's zero-shot findings. Not in runnable_models: LoRA or full fine-tuning of Chronos-2, and the TCN, LSTM and Transformer baselines trained per dataset; a daily 30 to 90 day protocol would also be a new protocol version.
